gaps.sentence: We had no ___ signed the lease than the landlord sold the building.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner … than' — here with 'had' before the participle.

gaps.sentence: Hardly had we left the house ___ it started to pour.
gaps.explanation: Hardly … when — fixed pair; 'than' belongs to 'no sooner'.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ she apologise, she also paid for the damage.
gaps.explanation: Not only did she…, (but) she also… — inversion after not only.

gaps.sentence: To ___ did you address that complaint, exactly?
Only by practising daily ___ you improve your fluency.
gaps.explanation: Only by doing X will you… — future inversion after only by.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ the tenders been opened when the leak was traced to the press office.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly had … been opened when' — past perfect passive with inversion.

gaps.sentence: Little ___ the villagers suspect that the mine would ever reopen.
gaps.explanation: 'Little did the villagers suspect' — they had no idea.

gaps.sentence: Not until the following morning ___ the damage reported to the police.
gaps.explanation: 'Not until + time' triggers inversion: 'was the damage reported'.
